title: 57-year-old unhoused person found dead in Charlottesville encampment - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Nadeau ,
4 hours ago
CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. (WRIC) — A 57-year-old unhoused person was found dead in an encampment beneath a Charlottesville bridge on Wednesday.
The morning of Wednesday, June 10, officers with the Charlottesville Police Department were called to the encampment beneath the Free Bridge following a report of “a strong odor” within one of the tents.
When they arrived, officers found a 57-year-old unhoused person inside the tent, deceased.
The identity of the unhoused person is being withheld until their loved ones can be notified.
Their cause and manner of death are currently under investigation. At this time, there are “no obvious signs of foul play,” according to police.
Three-vehicle crash in Henrico sends drivers to hospital “Today’s tragic discovery is a sobering reminder of the very real dangers faced by individuals living in this encampment,” said Charlottesville Chief of Police Mike Kochis in a press release .
The Charlottesville Police Department has reportedly been “conducting regular outreach” in this area over the past several weeks. These efforts will continue.
“The department remains committed to connecting vulnerable community members with available resources and services,” police said in the release.
No additional information on this tragic death is available as of the time of reporting.
